subject: Request: Temporary GPU capacity hold for Aurora Labs (AUR-4782)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Temporary GPU capacity hold for Aurora Labs (AUR-4782)

Team —

Aurora Labs is into late-stage procurement (deal AUR-4782). Eve (cc'd on the customer thread) has indicated they're likely to sign a pilot PO by Oct 30 with a go-live for a controlled pilot in the week of Nov 8. The ask from their side is for a guaranteed dedicated capacity window for the pilot so they can run sustained load tests.

Quick sizing summary they provided:
- Expected steady state: ~1,200 requests/sec (peak bursts to ~1,800)
- Concurrency target: ~200 concurrent sessions
- Latency SLO (99th pct): <150ms
- Estimated tokens/day: ~60M
- Preferred hardware: H100 (best), fallback A100-80GB (acceptable)

Action requested: can we place a provisional hold on capacity for this deal in our Dedicated pool (preferably dedicated-us-3) so we can guarantee the foil for the pilot while procurement finalizes the contract? Suggested hold window: 21 days from Oct 18 → Nov 8.

Operational constraints / asks for answers:
1) What exact GPU mix would you recommend to meet the SLO given our current inventory (H100 vs A100)?
2) Can we tag and lock nodes in dedicated-us-3 as a soft hold (non-billed) until the PO is signed, and if so what is the latest date we can do that?
3) Any concerns re: colocated vs cross-zone placements (they want low latency)?
4) If H100 are scarce, what's the recommended fallback configuration and the estimated perf delta?

I've attached the customer's sizing doc (capacity_estimate_AUR-4782.xlsx) and a compact summary they sent. Eve is asking for a written confirmation of a provisional hold by EOD Oct 18.

Thanks — please respond with availability and any blocking items.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-16T08:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary GPU capacity hold for Aurora Labs (AUR-4782)

Camila —

Thanks for the heads up. Inventory snapshot (as of 2026-10-16 07:30 PDT):
- Dedicated pool dedicated-us-3: 12x H100, 20x A100-80GB, 6x L40
- Currently reserved commitments overlapping Nov window: ~10 H100 equivalents reserved across two other pilots (one ends Nov 5, one ends Nov 12)

Preliminary sizing quick math: to hit ~1,200 rps with <150ms 99pct we estimate roughly 6 H100 equivalents for steady-state with room for bursts (this assumes optimized kernels and KV/prefix caching). If we use A100-80GB-only, we'd likely need ~10 nodes which increases cost and cross-zone routing risk.

Options:
A) Hold 6 H100 now in dedicated-us-3 (best perf) — we can mark these as a "proposal hold" in our capacity system (CS-7891) for up to 14 days by default; extension requires leadership sign-off.
B) Hold mix: 4 H100 + 6 A100 with co-location preference — gives more flexibility and reduces immediate H100 drawdown.
C) Hold A100-only: reserve 10 A100s but warn on latency headroom.

I can place an initial 14-day soft hold (no billing) today on the pool under CS-7891 with a note "AUR-4782 / Aurora pilot".

If we want 21 days we'll need Vivek to approve the extended provisional hold — otherwise the system will auto-release after 14 days.

No blockers from inventory perspective for a provisional hold, but two caveats:
- If other inbound commitments convert in the next 7 days we may need to renegotiate placement (we're tracking three other late-stage deals).
- If they insist on full H100-only for the entire pilot period we may have to propose staged onboarding (start with mixed fleet + upgrade to H100 if procurement accelerates).

Let me know which option you want me to apply to CS-7891.

Dylan
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-16T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary GPU capacity hold for Aurora Labs (AUR-4782)

Adding operational detail from the infra/ops side — thanks for initiating.

Notes and recommendations:
- For the 99th <150ms target we should ensure colocated nodes (same AZ) with enabled prefix KV cache and tuned batch concurrency. That reduces tokens-in-flight and latencies significantly.
- If they go H100-preferred, aim for 4-6 H100 in the same rack group + 6 A100 in the same AZ as a fallback. A mixed fleet (H100 + A100) with aggressive kernel selection should meet their SLO while we scale.
- We can prepare a minimal runbook for the pilot (autoscale thresholds, cache warm-up steps, telemetry hooks). I attached a short customer requirements summary (aurora_requirements_summary.pdf).

Operational asks for Camila:
1) Please confirm target pilot start window (they mentioned "week of Nov 8") — we need a calendar anchor to avoid overlap.
2) If you want the 21-day hold (Oct 18–Nov 8), have Vivek flag approval so Dylan can override the 14-day default.

If you give the go, I will open infra ticket INF-4612 to tag the nodes and pre-seed the caching layers; we'll also schedule a prepilot run with our SRE pairing two days prior to the start.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Dedicated Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-16T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary GPU capacity hold for Aurora Labs (AUR-4782)

All —

Approved: provisional 21-day hold for deal AUR-4782 in dedicated-us-3, effective Oct 18 → Nov 8, conditional on procurement signature and completion of the SOC2 evidence exchange window. Dylan: please create the hold under CS-7891 and set an internal escalator to me for any requests to extend beyond Nov 8. Marissa: please open INF-4612 and attach the runbook; coordinate the prepilot SRE pair.

Camila — tell the customer we will provisionally reserve capacity for the pilot pending PO. I've updated HubSpot (link below) with the hold note and assigned deal owner to you. Procurement must sign before we flip the hold to a billing-reserved state.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/AUR-4782
Mutual action plan: https://redwood.app/documents/AUR-4782/mutual-action-plan

I'll re-evaluate if we see competing confirmations from other pipeline deals. Thanks for moving quickly on this.
